<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**15** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **137** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 443b2f4fdce681f1d3656475c9c72f3ffacfee4c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0f91e546cad4e7469eb7b2b75d1d2d9cca5bb64c` — the merge of head `39379b9b98cecfcf76d28a291c4567184d9ec38f` into base `443b2f4fdce681f1d3656475c9c72f3ffacfee4c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0f91e546cad4e7469eb7b2b75d1d2d9cca5bb64c && git checkout 0f91e546cad4e7469eb7b2b75d1d2d9cca5bb64c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 443b2f4fdce681f1d3656475c9c72f3ffacfee4c 39379b9b98cecfcf76d28a291c4567184d9ec38f && git checkout -B drift-repro 443b2f4fdce681f1d3656475c9c72f3ffacfee4c && git merge --no-ff 39379b9b98cecfcf76d28a291c4567184d9ec38f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 443b2f4fdce681f1d3656475c9c72f3ffacfee4c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `39379b9b98cecfcf76d28a291c4567184d9ec38f`

Read: the PR body, diff (8 files, +871/−37), 4 commits and 35 check runs; card #19886 (body, all 34 comments; in particular `5805254639`, `5806608550`, `5853764742`, `5856326742`, `5857675669`, `5857706935`) and the 2a review `5806589396` on PR #19946; `cel-to-filter.ts`, `matches-filter.ts`, `rls-compiler.ts` 600–830, `security-plugin.ts` 3100–3290 and `getReadFilter`, `explain-engine.ts` 840–880, `having-filter.ts` 1060–1130, `bootstrap-declared-sharing-rules.ts` 100–330, `validate-rls-predicate-enforceability.ts` (probe and reference pass), `filter-comparand-shape.ts` 260–345, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, AGENTS.md 1060–1095, both changesets and both ADR-0087 entries. Ran, in a detached worktree at this head (deps built with turbo, 18 packages, exit 0; worktree removed): the PR's pins (formula 120, plugin-security 56); formula neighbours (9 files / 325); the 2a/2c/#20189/#20212 plugin-security pins (5 files / 111); lint RLS + sharing rule files (172); sharing-rule.test.ts; objectql having pair (56); `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main`, `check-changeset-no-major --base origin/main`, spec `check:migration-registry`; a 126-cell real-stack probe (SecurityPlugin + ObjectQL, driver-sql better-sqlite3 and driver-memory, json column + multiple lookup: 21 predicates × check-insert F/A × by-id-update F/A × using read + `getReadFilter`, with ground truth read as system); a lowering/evaluator probe over 17 refused spellings, 28 census strings and 10 boundary shapes; a sharing-bootstrap probe; a lint probe; an ablation of each face with the pins, restore proved by blob hash. NOT MEASURED: live mongod, PG, MySQL; driver-sqlite-wasm beyond the PR's own pin.

### ① Derived judgments

- **1. Fail-closed on every reachable door — RIGHT.** Every leak cell of `5806608550` and `5853764742` is refused through the real write check and the lowering, on both drivers, at both write doors (the dev measured inserts only; I added the by-id update, whose post-image merges the caller pre-image — driver-sql hands the json column back parsed, so the list is seen): (a) `record.status != record.tags`, `!(record.status == record.tags)`, the mirror `record.tags != record.status`, `record.reviewer != record.watchers` (multiple lookup) and `record.status > record.tags` → `INVALID_FILTER`/400 on the forbidden AND the allowed insert and update, nothing stored; (b) `!(record.status in [['closed','archived']])` and the host-staged `!(record.status in current_user.nested_set)`, (c) `record.status > ['m']`, `≤ ['m']` (the `$lte` spelling), `> current_user.org_user_ids`, `current_user.org_user_ids > 'a'`, (d) `record.reviewer > current_user`, (e) `current_user.org_user_ids != 'x'` → `PERMISSION_DENIED`/403 on every write, nothing stored; `using` reads return zero rows and `getReadFilter` hands the analytics bridge `RLS_DENY_FILTER`. No leak cell admits. Loud: a literal form WARNs `[RLS] … has an uncompilable predicate … DROPPED` on every compile (b1, c1, c3, d1); a resolved form WARNs `[RLS] DENY (fail closed): … (unsupported): the detail` when the request denies (b3, c4, c5, e1); (a) is a thrown 400 with the constant message. The before-table re-checked against the dev's `cells-before.json` (a1/b1/c4/d1/e1 admitted+stored at `3cb84d08`; d1 already 403 on merged main via #20212) and `cells-head.json` — consistent with my readings. The one door that stays permissive is declared, not this PR's: (a) at the driver-memory `using` read returns every row, exactly as the LEGAL control `record.status != record.reviewer` does there (driver-memory never evaluates `{ $field }`), pointer on #15104 (item ③).
- **2. No over-refusal — RIGHT.** Census: 613 `using`/`check`/sharing-`condition` string occurrences across objectstack `39379b9b` + cloud `48d7066` (regex over every non-`node_modules` `.ts/.js/.json/.yaml/.md*`), 278 non-test; the 28 distinct authored predicates among them (all `default-permission-sets.ts` spellings, `rls.zod.ts` examples, `verify/rls.ts`, `security-plugin.ts:3144`, showcase `permission-sets.ts` and `sharing-rules.ts`, docs, skills, the qa fixture; cloud carries only `id == current_user.id` in tests and no `rowLevelSecurity`) all pass `isPushdownableCel` and `compileCelToFilter` with a realistic `current_user`; `validateRlsPredicateEnforceability` over the shipped 107 default policies: 0 findings. On the real stack the six named neighbours are accepted and enforced on both drivers: `record.status != 'closed'` (F 403 / A stored / reads `r_archived,r_open`), `record.status != record.reviewer` (F 403 / A stored / driver-sql reads `r_archived,r_open`), `!(record.status in ['closed','archived'])`, `record.status > 'm'`, `record.reviewer == current_user.id` (reads `r_open`), `record.reviewer in current_user.org_user_ids` (reads `r_archived,r_open`); the compound `!(record.status in current_user.org_user_ids) && record.status > 'm'` lowers. A legal `$or` branch still admits: `record.reviewer == current_user.id || record.status != record.tags` admits the row the caller reviews (short-circuit before the refused arm) and 400s the other — logically right.
- **3. The `{ $field }` check — RIGHT, and correctly per record.** `assertComparableReference` runs in `evalOp` before `resolveValue`, only for `$eq/$ne/$gt/$gte/$lt/$lte`, and tests `getPath(record, $field)` and `actual` with `Array.isArray || plain-object` (`Date` excluded), so both sides are judged (mirror a5 and `record.status > record.tags` measured refused) and the `addDays` form is judged on its base before the `NO_OFFSET_BASE` sentinel a `$not` would invert (pinned). A `null` or absent referent is NOT refused and compares as before (`$ne` → true; measured) — correct, a missing value is one value. Callers: four in production — `security-plugin.ts:3167` (RLS check, the target), `:3438` (tenant wall, platform-derived `organization_id` filters, never a `{ $field }`), `explain-engine.ts:872` (RLS-compiled filter per record: a record whose compared column holds a list now makes explain throw 400 where it answered before — a real but undeclared move, item ③), `having-filter.ts:1117` (a three-column probe `{ value, referent }` → on driver-memory a list-holding groupBy/aggregate column is now refused 400; driver-sql rows carry JSON text and compare as before). The having move is correct — refusing beats coercing a list, matches the evaluator's contract — and is declared under `@objectstack/objectql`; the having pair (56) is green.
- **4. plugin-sharing — RIGHT on all three.** `celToFilterOutcome` compiles with `variables: {}` and returns `{ filter: null, cause: { reason: 'unsupported', detail } }` for `record.status > ['m']`, `!(record.status in [['closed']])`, `['a'] != 'x'`; `bootstrapDeclaredSharingRules` then `continue`s without `defineRule` (measured: 2 skipped, 1 seeded, `defineRule` called once for `record.status == 'new'`) — fail CLOSED, no grant, no over-share (ADR-0049). Logged: `logger.warn('[sharing-rule] skipped (missing or untranslatable CEL condition — never seeded as match-all)', { rule, condition, reason: 'unsupported', detail })` measured on both skips. Declared: the changeset's `@objectstack/plugin-sharing` bullet.
- **5. Sentences — TRUE for every refused class, one precision flag.** The widened `arrayComparandError` names each class the shape walk and the per-record arm refuse (`$ne`, equality, ordering, `$in`/`$nin` member, `{ $field }` list-or-object either side), its remedies, and the measured failure directions; it names no field, operator or value (pinned with secret columns). 2a's changeset and its registry entry `rls-predicate-array-comparand-refused` (`replacement`: "{ $field } references evaluate exactly as before") are now FALSE for a list- or object-holding column; the 2d changeset states the delta in one sentence and the 2d entry's `replacement` restricts the claim to "single-valued columns" — correct. The 2a entry text itself is not corrected (item ③). Precision flag on the `@objectstack/lint` bullet, "an ordering comparison against a membership set through the reference pass": measured true only opposite a field (`record.reviewer_id > current_user.org_user_ids` → `rls-predicate-unenforceable`); the constant-branch forms `current_user.org_user_ids > 'a'` / `!= 'x'` / `== 'u'` are silent at `os validate` (no lowered field site for the swap to attribute) and are refused per request at runtime with the DENY WARN. Non-blocking: the PR body's "resolved values are refused per request" covers them, the runtime is fail-closed, and the lint file is #20158's.
- **6. Pins — RIGHT; one flip, declared.** Formula: every refused literal form asserted `unsupported` + shape-refused + `isSupportedRlsExpression` false; every resolved form `unsupported` with the shape passing, the variable PATH named and five secrets withheld; each remedy; neighbours (one bound, flat `in`, scalar folds, field-to-field `==`/`!=`). Evaluator: the `SHAPES` table gains the four ordering ops and `$in`/`$nin` members, run at every depth, empty array and every record; a per-record describe (both sides, negated, ordering, object, offset form, under `$or`) with a one-value control and a withholding check. plugin-security: leak × door (check F/A with `stored()`, using read, `getReadFilter` deny) × 2 drivers, plus four enforced controls. Flip: `{ tags: { $eq: { $field: 'tags' } } }` true → 400, declared in the PR body and the test comment; its two scalar lines kept. No other pin moved: 325 formula, 111 sibling plugin-security, 172 lint, 116 sharing, 56 having green. Ablation from this head: evaluator cut (3 arms) → 57/120 formula red, 8/56 plugin-security red (exactly the four (a) write rows × 2 drivers); lowering cut (4 anchors) → 25/120 red, 28/56 red (every (b)/(c)/(e) row; (d) stays green because #20212's `judgeCompiledComparands` drops it independently); restore → both blobs equal HEAD (`1fb6f28c…`, `4c6ef215…`), rebuilt, 120/120 and 56/56. Identical to the dev's numbers.

### ② Semver level

- **`minor` + BREAKING — RIGHT.** The diff narrows two published accept sets (`compileCelToFilter`, `matchesFilterCondition`); AGENTS.md:1075 makes `(narrowing)` BREAKING, and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` records the launch-window convention that a breaking change ships as `minor` with the `**BREAKING**` banner and the ADR-0087 disposition as the carriers. The changeset has all three; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` matches the 2a round-0 precedent and #19882. `check-changeset-no-major --base origin/main` exits 0 (no major; level axis N/A locally, `Check Changeset` success in CI).
- **Packages — RIGHT.** `@objectstack/formula` (source), `@objectstack/spec: patch` (a new entry + regenerated registry, the 2a precedent), and four behaviour-moving packages with no source change (`plugin-security`, `plugin-sharing`, `lint`, `objectql`) — the 2a review's own non-blocking asked for exactly this ("its CHANGELOG will carry no sentence for the 400 an upgrading agent greps; add it to the same changeset"). All six are in the `fixed` group (69), so no version is moved that would not have moved.
- **`registered` — RIGHT.** `18.cel-predicate-one-value-comparand-refused.ts` is new in this diff, resolves at HEAD, and `check-adr-0087-registration --base origin/main` reads `registered cel-predicate-one-value-comparand-refused (new here)`; `check:migration-registry`: current (265 semantic). The entry's `surface`/`replacement`/`reason`/`acceptanceCriteria` name every refused shape and the FROM → TO rewrite, and it correctly adds no D2 conversion (the platform cannot tell which comparison a predicate stood in for).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **(d)/(e) fold, for the director's 追认.** All four in-place conditions hold on my reading: same class (a comparand that is not one value), the fix is the #20189 guard's operator condition dropped plus the constant branch's list arm (one function each), `cel-to-filter.ts` is on claim `5856326742`, same gates and pins; both were measured live at `3cb84d08` before the edit (admitted+stored; allow-all). On merged main #20212's RLS-compiler faces already drop (d) — the changeset says so, and the lowering-cut ablation shows it (the (d) rows stay green). The fold is declared in the PR body, the dev report's `deviations`, and the seat's ACCEPT; the record only notes that ratification is not this review's to grant.
- **Remainder doors, both declared.** (a) at the driver-memory `using` read: every row for a1/a2/a5/a6 AND for the legal control `record.status != record.reviewer` (the driver never evaluates `{ $field }`; the analytics ObjectQL strategy on memory inherits it) — a frozen test/demo driver, pointer on #15104 per the seat. (a) at the compile door: `record.status != record.tags` still lowers and lint is clean (measured); the lowering holds column names only (`RlsFieldGuard`), so the authoring arm belongs to the lint rule, serial after #20158 (seat ruled A). Also silent at lint, and in the same bucket: the constant-branch membership forms (c4, e1) — runtime refuses per request.
- **`compileScopedFilterToSql` binding a list** under an ordering operator: declared in the acceptance notes; unreachable from RLS now (the lowering drops the policy → deny scope), reachable only from a host-supplied `getReadScope`. Not measured here.
- **Shared faces passing an array under ordering and a nested `$in` member:** `filter-comparand-shape.ts:339` carves them out by name ("same class, recorded on the card, scoped separately"); every driver refuses them on its own (dev's cells-before `using_sql`/`using_memory` 400 for c1); no RLS path reaches them now. Note: #20212's `judgeCompiledComparands` in the RLS compiler ALREADY refuses an OBJECT member of a host-staged membership set (`!(record.status in current_user.obj_set)` with `obj_set: [{a:1}]` → `refused-comparand`, 403 / no rows — measured), though the raw evaluator still answers `{ $not: { s: { $in: [{a:1}] } } }` true and the lowering emits it; closed at the RLS door, JSON-only elsewhere.
- **Merge with open PR #20251** (`71ea994d`): `git merge-tree` clean; both PRs add a semantic entry and regenerate `registry.ts`; the second to land regenerates. Also clean against current `origin/main` `443b2f4f` (9 commits past the merge-base, none touching formula). Head unchanged at report time; `mergeable_state: clean`; CI 30 success / 5 skipped (Auto Label, Check PR Size, Console Pin Gate, Build Docs, opt-in pack smoke) / 0 failing, all required contexts green.
- **Anything else, none blocking:**
  - Stored-side list under an ordering operator with a literal bound: `{ tags: ['m'] }` vs `{ tags: { $gt: 'a' } }` answers true by string coercion (measured), i.e. `record.tags > 'a'` on a json column still coerces at the write check while driver-sql compares the JSON text on the read — the mirror of (c) with the list on the RECORD side. Outside (c)'s letter (the comparand is one value), and 2a pinned the stored side as untouched for equality; but the new `{ $field }` arm refuses the stored side only when the comparand is a reference, an asymmetry the seat may want to rule on. Census: 0 producers order on a json/multiple column.
  - `addDays` referencing a list column under `$not` admits (NaN offset → `NO_OFFSET_BASE` → false → inverted); JSON-only — the CEL lowering refuses `addDays()` as an unsupported call.
  - explain-engine (`explain-engine.ts:872`): a `{ $field }` RLS filter judged on a record whose compared column holds a list now throws 400 from explain; a behaviour move the changeset does not name (2a's did).
  - The 2a registry entry `rls-predicate-array-comparand-refused` still says `{ $field }` references "evaluate exactly as before" (protocol major 18, unreleased); the 2d changeset states the delta, the seat holds the deliberate-correction carrier.
  - The `having` half face on driver-sql compares the stored JSON text of a list column as before (declared) — one predicate, two answers across the two drivers; the driver-memory freeze covers it.
